newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to tighten import quality controls.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to tighten import quality controls.

text.p: Vietnam, facing problems with a ballooning trade deficit, said on Wednesday it would require tighter quality control checks on selected categories of imported goods beginning in January.

An official with the Government Measures, Standardisation and Quality Department told Reuters the move would affect a range of commodities including foodstuffs, cement, fertilisers, insecticides and electronic equipment.
The official said the decision was in line with existing government regulations, and was aimed at protecting the interests of the state and of consumers.
"The impact it will have on the quantity of goods being imported to Vietnam will depend on the Ministry of Trade...," he said.
Trade Ministry officials were not available to comment.
The reasons behind the move were not immediately clear and economists in Hanoi said it was too early to gauge whether the move was aimed at addressing broader trade problems.
Vietnam reported a record trade deficit of $3.591 billion in the period from January 1 to November 15 this year. The trade deficit for the whole of 1995 was $2.3 billion.
According to data from a recent U.N. report, that puts Vietnam's trade gap in the region of an unsustainable 15-19 percent of gross domestic product.

Economists are concerned about the problem, and about indications that Vietnam may be losing its enthusiasm for trade liberalisation. But they also note that export growth is currently around 30 percent.
Gross official reserves are also continuing to grow.
In March last year, Vietnam's reserves were put at $1.0 billion. Hanoi has not issued updated figures, but central bank officials have indicated a current level of around $1.6 billion.
According to legislation issued in December last year, government ministries will be responsible for the quality checking process.
